title: `ensureObjectStorage`'s `'objects'` limb is now dormant — a spelling-tolerant lookup one layer below the `/meta` fold
body:
Blocked-by: #8769

Observation recorded while implementing #8769. Dormant code, not a defect — filed so the sweep is on record rather than acted on.

## What was measured

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:11291`:

```ts
private async ensureObjectStorage(type: string, name: string): Promise {
    if (type !== 'object' && type !== 'objects') return;
```

It has exactly two call sites, and after #8769 both stand behind the `/meta` boundary fold:

- `:12135` — inside `saveMetaItem`, which folds at `:11375`.
- `:12966` — inside `runPublishSideEffects`, reached only from `publishMetaItem`, which folds at `:12703` as of #8769.

So `type` is canonical at both, and the `type === 'objects'` limb can no longer be reached. Before #8769 the second call site could still deliver `'objects'` — which is why the limb was doing real work there and why its removal was not correct to fold into that PR.

## Why it is worth recording rather than leaving

It is precisely the shape `canonicalMetaType`'s header rejects, in that header's own words:

> Do not "fix" a future instance of this by teaching a predicate one layer down (`isNestedArtifactField` and friends) to accept a plural. That is the spelling-tolerant lookup this comment has rejected since #4432.

A tolerant predicate below a boundary that already folds is not merely dead — it is a standing invitation to address the layer directly and conclude that tolerance one level down is the house style. #7894's four manifest-absent types are what that habit costs when the tolerance and the fold disagree about which map is authoritative.

## Suggested disposition

Drop the `&& type !== 'objects'` limb, leaving `if (type !== 'object') return;`. No behaviour change is expected (see the reachability measurement above), so the pin that matters is the existing publish/save coverage staying green, not a new one.

⚠️ Verify the reachability claim on the tree of the day before removing: a new caller added between now and then would make the limb live again, and this finding's whole basis is that there are exactly two callers and both fold.

Backlink: #8769 (which added the second fold and left this comment in place at `:12685`).
